chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from a man

bought a slave girl on the condition that she was a virgin, but he did not find her to be a virgin. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The excess of the value is returned to him when it is known that he is truthful.'

key_terms.فَضْلُ الْقِيمَة: excess of the value / price difference

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning the price difference if a bought slave girl is not found to be a virgin as stipulated?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'khiyar al-shart' (option of condition) in slave sales, emphasizing that compensation is limited to the difference in value rather than full rescission, provided the buyer's claim of truthfulness is verified. It reflects the Shia juristic focus on fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring the seller is not unjustly enriched while protecting the buyer from hidden defects. The ruling underscores the importance of evidentiary verification in resolving disputes over stipulated attributes in pre-modern Islamic markets.
